reviews.comment: Ivan can't lecture. He goes off into his own world doing a made up problem, skips steps, messes up, and has to do it all again. The was always a collective confusion. He's bad as well one on one, consult anyone else for help. He does curve quite a bit. Use recitation, the supplemental materials, SI, and the book to get through it, you'll be fine.

Ivan is someone who knows the physics concepts in his head but a lot of the times it is so hard to understand what he is trying to say. In addition, he will always get confused when writing super tiny on the whiteboard that he will have to go back and redo what he wrote. Also, his problems are all hypothetical so just do the recitation problems.

Good guy but not a good lecturer. Always seems disorganized and pretty much every class he does 1-2 example problems, but makes mistakes and asks the class where he messed up. 

You don't really learn anything from lecture. Tests make up 90% of the grade, no attendance, no homework. Purposefully makes exam problems wordy for the final.

He is getting better as a professor but he still mumbles and his teaching is often confusing. He either writes too much down and makes the board a complete confusing mess or he skips important steps at the beginning. The only way I could get a decent understanding of the material was to go to every SI session.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is awful at lecturing, often confuses himself and asks the class whether he is correct or not. He often skips over several steps and doesn't elaborate on those steps. Does not use actual exam questions to teach the material, he instead makes up hypotheticals and assumes a lot of things to even get the answer. Do not take him unless you need to.

Borzenets is a nice guy and pretty entertaining, but he simply isn't all that great at lecturing. He often comes up with problems on the spot, and spends the rest of lecture trying to solve them, not really having the class engage at all. However this class as a whole isn't terribly difficult, just go to S.I. and practice previous exams.

Horrible teacher, spends most of his time mumbling and confusing himself on problems that he invents on the spot. Unless you want to fully teach yourself with the help of SI sessions and recitations do not take. No homework, three tests and a final count for 20% each. The final can be 100% of grade if the grade is better than your total average.

He's a nice guy but an awful professor. His lectures are disorganized, and he sometimes works out the problems incorrectly. It's tough to follow along with the lecture as he skips many steps and explains things as if you should know them already. SI sessions can save your grade but try to avoid this professor if possible as you will learn little.
does not explain things well, hard to read notes on the board unless you are in the first 5 rows, no homework but exams take up TONS of points and theyre hard. SI is a lifesaver
I learned from him a lot.

Mr. Borzenets has been the worst professor I have had at Texas A&M. This is also the most poorly organized course I have ever taken. He has only entered one grade into canvas the entire semester as of writing this, so I do not even know what grade I have. This professor has truly baffled me with how little effort he has shown. Wish I could say more

Not the greatest at teaching but really cares. If you go to office hours he will work with you. Its not an easy class but its do able. Check over exams after they are graded, gradescope has issues. Iffy on email response time.

It was his first semester teaching at A&M and this course already has a clear curriculum with plenty of outside materials. His lectures were passionate, but I did not find them useful. Your grade is based purely on how you perform on tests, so make use of the previous exams. Also the textbook is a great resource & easy to read, but not mandatory.

This class is very difficult, Prof. Borzenets is in his first year as a prof at TAMU though so some of the course roughness is understandable. The class demonstrations are very interesting and good. The lectures are very complicated so going to recitation is VERY important.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This was Ivan's first semester at A&M. He seems like a really kind person and you could tell he cares about his students, but I stopped going to class and just watched Tatiana's videos because she explained the concepts better. He did curve the final grade though which came in clutch.

His don't panic course is flat out difficult to understand however it is his very first year and I feel this school and students who want amazing professors put him down. He really tried to show you applications of physics in the real world and put effort into bringing different physical examples into the class each and every day.
